response.message: Here's what I heard: on AWS, we predict equipment maintenance needs from synthetic sensor histories and maintenance records, and the result is only a work-order draft that an operator reviews. Nothing controls the equipment automatically. I've drawn the full flow on the board: Kinesis and IoT Core for sensor ingestion, S3 for history, Glue for feature preparation, SageMaker for training, held-out evaluation and the Model Registry, a batch scoring job, Model Monitor for drift, and a Lambda that writes work-order drafts to DynamoDB for operator review. Only the S3 storage has native Terraform coverage today. The other components are design-only and still need engineering. Nothing is deployed, and I haven't checked any region or account access. The first local test runs the flow on synthetic fixtures with a scripted, mocked model. That shows the wiring and payloads work end to end, but it says nothing about how accurate the model is. Real model validation needs SageMaker training and a time-based held-out evaluation against real failure labels. How should we define a maintenance "need" for the model to learn? For example, "a failure within the next 7 days" or "a maintenance record within 14 days".

proposal.title: AWS predictive maintenance end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic sensor and maintenance data → features → SageMaker training/evaluation/registry → batch scoring → drift monitoring → operator-reviewed work-order drafts. Assumptions: region to be selected; batch scoring; no equipment control. Only S3 has native generator coverage; other services are design-only and require engineering. Nothing is deployed or verified.

data.label: Synthetic sensor generator
data.description: Existing synthetic sensor source publishing telemetry over MQTT.

data.label: Sensor ingestion
data.description: Receives telemetry and uses a rule to route it to Kinesis Data Firehose, which delivers it to S3. Firehose is shown inside this component.

data.label: Synthetic maintenance records
data.description: Existing CSV export of synthetic maintenance and failure history, used as labels.

data.label: Raw and curated data
data.description: Private, versioned, encrypted bucket for raw telemetry, maintenance records, features and model artifacts.

data.label: Feature preparation
data.description: Builds windowed sensor features and time-aligned failure labels, avoiding leakage, and writes the results to S3.

data.label: Training and held-out evaluation
data.description: Trains the model, then evaluates it on a later held-out time window (precision/recall and false alarms) before registration.

data.label: Versioned model
data.description: Holds versioned model packages with evaluation metrics; a person approves promotion.

data.label: Maintenance risk scoring
data.description: Scores the latest features with the approved model version and outputs failure risk for each asset.

data.label: Drift monitoring
data.description: Compares scored data with the training baseline and raises alerts through CloudWatch.

data.label: Work-order drafts
data.description: Turns risk above a threshold into idempotent draft work orders stored in DynamoDB. Drafts only; never controls equipment.

data.label: Maintenance operator
data.description: A person who reviews, approves or rejects each draft.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Random splits leak future data and overstate accuracy; mocks prove nothing about quality.
requirementDrafts.statement: Model versions are evaluated on a time-based held-out window before registry approval; acceptance thresholds to be agreed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Sensor behaviour changes silently degrade predictions.
requirementDrafts.statement: Feature and prediction drift on scored data is monitored against the training baseline, with alerts to the model owner.

response.message: The emulation run has no failures: the design wires up end to end, and every blocker is unfinished work, not something broken. The first one we can act on is the "Raw and curated data" bucket, which has no defined access. We need to decide which existing identity uploads the maintenance-records CSV, because I can then add a scoped read/write grant for that identity only. The other blockers, from ingestion through scoring, need product engineering (native generators for IoT Core, Glue and SageMaker), and a diagram edit can't fix that. Who uploads the synthetic maintenance CSV today: an existing AWS IAM role or user in this account, or a person who uploads it by hand? A minimal need would be read/write access for documents in this bucket only.
